title: The Karmic Theory of Inequality
content: This paper introduces the Karmic Theory of Inequality (KTI) with the formal explanation for the persistence of individual differences through the lens of Buddhist philosophy. The theory conceptualizes inequality as the cumulative outcome of intended actions expressed in physical (P), verbal (V), and thought (T) modalities, each weighted by a causal-intentional function (I). Using logical reasoning and mathematical proof, we demonstrate that no two individuals can have identical intentions across the infinite lifecycle of past and present moments. Differences in lifespan, health, wealth, beauty, wisdom, and social status are inevitable regardless of external conditions or interventions. This theory provides a fresh perspective on why inequality remains a constant feature of societies. The KTI is original in proving the certainty of inequality among individuals and species.
